shoal_e13_entry.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_entry.text: On Day Three Hundred Fourteen, Yue went to her own ordinary clinical review before the property inventory. She paid the stated two-copper follow-up fee from money already received. The elbow remained tender; touch, grip, and leg checks showed no new reported change beyond the bruise's current course. The practitioner continued the no-load and no-powered-work restriction until the next actual review. Yue left with a body limit, not a failed cultivation stage, and walked to the public receiving desk.

shoal_e13_receiving_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_receiving_01.text: Han had prepared a new paid term because the town's owner receiving would continue longer than a heroic afternoon. The Post-Fire Receiving Account held two hundred forty copper from its newly named appropriation. One hundred fifty paid Yue's thirty five-copper four-hour receiving shifts across six weeks, sixty paid two qualified ordinary pattern readers thirty each, eighteen funded permitted tags and closures, and twelve the defined messages. The old restoration account stayed closed.

shoal_e13_receiving_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_receiving_02.text: Yue's offered job covered reading permitted owner statements, witnessing actual custody receiving, and recording decisions under the proper readers. It excluded load handling and powered examination. Her restricted elbow could fit that work if she rested as advised and reported changed symptoms. The two pattern readers had ordinary material qualifications, not hidden authority over her cultivation. They would assess the surviving tool drawings or mould condition within their actual expertise and owner permissions.

shoal_e13_receiving_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_receiving_03.text: The accepted days ran from Day Three Hundred Fourteen through Three Hundred Fifty-Five, thirty performed shifts with six weekly twenty-five-copper settlements. The first four-hour interval began after her clinical review. An unperformed shift would need an honest later agreement; the printed target did not pay itself. She accepted the narrow term. It gave her livelihood while people made decisions about real losses, without making her arm part of the town's reconstruction budget.

shoal_e13_receiving_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_receiving_04.text: The first pattern reader had ink on a thumb and refused to wear the ceremonial sash a clerk offered for public receiving. He said the sash would catch a rough wooden edge and the owners needed a current qualification mark, not a costume. The second brought a clean ordinary measuring set under her own tool inventory. Yue liked them before they agreed on anything. Their expertise appeared in particular objections rather than a claim that everything could now be repaired.

shoal_e13_receiving_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_receiving_05.text: At the public boundary, the fire crew opened only the specified cool approach. Marked hot pockets and unstable supports remained excluded. Owners gave their current location information to the qualified inventory team and waited outside. Yue's paid receiving task stayed at the safe table, with her arm supported. Her certificate did not qualify her to reach under a charred beam. The actual source of today's facts would be the people who had permission and safe conditions to inspect them.

shoal_e13_receiving_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_receiving_06.text: The private-tool owner involved in the assault had a separate permitted inventory request. The ordinary watch process continued under its own authority. He would not accompany Yue or enter unsupervised. A current lawful representative could identify his tools through the accompanied inventory if accepted by the responsible keeper. His family chose such a representative. The bruise did not erase property rights, and the property request did not erase the offered assault account.

shoal_e13_receiving_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_receiving_07.text: He Ming arrived for the workers who had asked him to read public updates. He left private family documents in their owners' hands. The initial safe receiving count would separate intact objects, damaged objects needing further judgment, and confirmed losses. No category would promise compensation before a source and scope existed. Some listeners wanted a single disaster total. The actual people needed narrower numbers to decide whether their next work could proceed.

shoal_e13_receiving_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_receiving_08.text: Yue drew the columns slowly with her left hand while keeping the bruised elbow supported. The handwriting looked unlike her usual notes. Han checked the figures with her before any posted extract left the table. A changed body could introduce ordinary record mistakes even in a task that did not involve lifting. The correction step mattered. She would not treat a paid reader's pride as a reason to make the first awkward number permanent.

shoal_e13_receiving_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_receiving_09.text: At the guarded keeper's shelf and the cooled wreck approach, the material preserved by her emergency role had different current states. Eight tool-drawing bundles or thirty provisional moulds and four visibly cracked pieces had reached custody; the opposite place had burned or remained inaccessible. Today's qualified review would verify condition and loss. Yue could not use relief from an exterior rescue count to fill an internal condition field before the owner opened it.

shoal_e13_receiving_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_receiving_10.text: The pattern readers checked their separate offered scopes with the owners. A drawing might be technically readable and still not offered for publication. A mould might look intact and fail a working condition review. Confirmed loss of a private annotation would not erase every retained base pattern or remembered skill elsewhere. Each distinction mattered because the town's next choices depended on what remained, what could be newly made, and who had authority to decide.

shoal_e13_receiving_11.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_receiving_11.text: Outside the receiving lane, a boy watched a crow carry a small charred chip onto the public wall. He wanted to keep it as a fire relic. The teacher asked him not to take unidentified material from the guarded site and found an ordinary clean shell for his current art instead. The crow flew off without a lesson. Yue smiled at a creature that could inhabit the town's disaster without knowing anyone's record categories.

shoal_e13_receiving_12.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_receiving_12.text: When the first actual owner review was ready, Yue put the clean receiving page beneath its proper label. She would record what qualified eyes and lawful owners established, not what her earlier support group had hoped. The fire's material outcome would now become specific enough to hurt differently. She waited as the keeper brought the surviving property or the permitted loss report to the safe table.

shoal_e13_material_gate.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_material_gate.text: The qualified property review followed the support role actually completed under the fire plan. The safe table held its appropriate source, with owners present or represented under current authority. Yue's elbow stayed supported and no energy entered the material. She would witness a real condition and custody decision, leaving absent or destroyed work absent rather than rebuilding it in the account.

shoal_e13_records_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_records_01.text: The keeper received each owner's current opening permission separately before breaking a seal. The four custodians who had walked the long route did not own all eight drawings. Some represented others under written current authority; one owner attended in person; another offered a remote permission through the declared ordinary receiving. Yue witnessed the offered authority and left unoffered papers unopened. The count could be completed without making private work publicly available.

shoal_e13_records_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_records_02.text: Seven drawings and their unique annotations were fully readable under the qualified ordinary review. The eighth retained its base tool pattern but had a heat-darkened edge that erased five small handwritten revisions before or during its removal. The reader could not certify those exact lost words from shape or smell. Eight bundles had reached custody, and seven whole annotated surfaces plus one partial surface had survived. The condition result narrowed the earlier exterior success rather than contradicting it.

shoal_e13_records_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_records_03.text: The eighth owner remembered some intended measurements but declined to call a new note his lost original. He would compare retained ordinary work and write a dated reconstruction if he chose. Yue recorded the distinction. No qi reading recovered the erased ink. The owner was alive and skilled, which offered real work ahead; it did not make the old five annotations intact. His wife said he had never trusted his handwriting anyway, and he laughed without ceasing to grieve it.

shoal_e13_records_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_records_04.text: The two ordinary readers separated readable geometry from permission to copy. Three owners allowed narrow comparative extracts for a later offered worker lesson. Others kept their annotations private. All retained their originals under the custody decisions they actually chose. A drawing's survival did not bind its owner to educate the port as payment for rescue. Yue could accept a publicly useful result from some people while protecting a refusal from others.

shoal_e13_records_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_records_05.text: One readable sheet showed a clamp its maker had altered after an old wrist problem. Its annotation described the ordinary handle position, not an energy route or a clinical treatment. The maker allowed the reader to explain that permitted feature to the current receiving group and withheld a personal note beneath it. The explanation mattered to later tool work. The private sentence mattered to someone too, and need not become technical evidence merely because it shared the same paper.

shoal_e13_records_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_records_06.text: The qualified wreck crew confirmed no working hardwood compression moulds from the opposite burned bay were recoverable. All thirty-four original wooden forms had burned or failed condition beyond current working use. Nine ordinary iron base pieces survived in owner-marked wreck material, subject to their separate qualified review. The iron did not restore the vanished cut faces. Mould owners could decide later what new tools could be made from different resources.

shoal_e13_records_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_records_07.text: A mould worker heard that seven whole drawings had survived and asked whether they included his particular shapes. Most did not. The saved unpowered tool patterns belonged to their stated owners and tasks. One offered clamp note might help a future workshop, but it did not contain every missing compression surface. Yue explained the actual scope with the reader beside her. The worker could want the papers useful and still learn that his own first need remained unmet.

shoal_e13_records_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_records_08.text: He chose to keep his permitted claim focused on the thirty-four wooden forms rather than seize another owner's drawing as a substitute. His ordinary craft memory remained, along with some external base records, but making new shapes would take time and money. He had lost working stock, not every thought. The fire's cost lay partly in having to do new labor for results that yesterday had stood ready on a shelf.

shoal_e13_records_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_records_09.text: The reader assessed the nine iron bases only within his qualified ordinary material scope. Several needed later cleaning and checks before reuse, and no fueled apparatus permission attached to any of them. Owners retained the decision whether to pay that work or dispose of a piece properly. Yue did not handle the hot-site material. Her receiving note could describe offered decisions without making a restricted arm the instrument that established them.

shoal_e13_records_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_records_10.text: At the safe table, the owner of the partial drawing authorized a dated note of the five lost revisions' known subjects, leaving uncertain values blank. The note was new and incomplete. It could guide a later permitted comparison without pretending to recover exact ink. Yue used the owner-approved wording and kept his private family discussion absent. The receiving job gave her a task she could finish honestly even when the object itself stayed partly unresolved.

shoal_e13_records_11.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_records_11.text: One of the fully readable owners chose to take her original home under its proper receiving procedure. The keeper checked the actual identity and marked custody ended for that bundle. Another chose finite locked storage while arranging a workshop. The different decisions meant eight saved bundles would not remain one display for visitors. Rescue had restored owners' choices rather than creating a permanent public cabinet whose openness proved the helper's virtue.

shoal_e13_records_12.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_records_12.text: The long-route custodian returned the shared cabinet key to its lawful holder after the last relevant receiving. It had opened a real lock under a safe plan and would still open whatever cabinet arrangement the owners used next. It was no mystical reward. Yue watched the metal change ordinary hands and remembered its marks in the frightened woman's palm. The useful action had been permission and movement, not possession of an extraordinary object.

shoal_e13_records_13.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_records_13.text: A public notice stated the condition counts and offered safety scope without publishing private patterns. Seven full annotated drawings and one partial were in actual owner custody; zero working wooden moulds remained from the burned bay; nine iron base pieces awaited or underwent their separate checks. The notice did not call the overall loss small. Each number supported a different possible next task and a different owner who could accept or refuse it.

shoal_e13_records_14.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_records_14.text: Rong read the public counts and asked whether newly made moulds could be ordered by next week. The owners and qualified readers named realistic ordinary lead times and current missing resources. He disliked the answer but did not invent Yue as a faster manufacturer. Her small-talisman qualification concerned a marker. Rebuilding thirty-four compression forms was ordinary material work requiring skilled hands, accepted specifications, and money he would need to find under a new contract.

shoal_e13_records_15.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_records_15.text: At the end of her receiving interval, Yue put the permitted owner decisions in their proper files and left the private originals with their chosen keepers. The seven complete annotation surfaces could support later work where owners offered it. The five lost revisions and the burned wooden forms remained lost. She had been paid to make that current picture usable, not to make it happy. The bruised elbow let her finish only because the task had been designed for reading.

shoal_e13_records_16.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_records_16.text: The mould worker who had refused conversation before now asked whether she could carry his public loss question to He Ming's offered desk. She accepted that narrow message, leaving him free to withhold anything private. It was not forgiveness for her support choice, and she did not ask for it. The material result had made a new ordinary interaction possible. They could work on a next question while disagreeing about the route that had preceded the loss.

shoal_e13_moulds_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_moulds_01.text: The thirty provisional working moulds and four visibly cracked pieces were laid out by authorized ordinary handlers, not by Yue's restricted arm. Each carried its actual owner mark. The qualified readers checked condition within the relevant ordinary tool specifications. A salvaged piece's beauty or old family use did not buy a pass. The owners watched from the safe side, asking questions they had prepared during two nights of uncertainty.

shoal_e13_moulds_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_moulds_02.text: Twenty-eight wooden moulds passed the current ordinary working-condition review. Two of the thirty provisional pieces were warped and required a separately approved adaptation before any stated working use. The four visibly cracked pieces remained out of use under their owners' proper decision process. Thirty-four objects had reached custody; twenty-eight usable, two pending, and four rejected were the actual result. The provisional exterior count had been a first state, not a promise of thirty complete tools.

shoal_e13_moulds_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_moulds_03.text: One owner wanted to use a warped piece gently until its adaptation could be paid. The qualified reader explained the relevant current failure condition and refused that working signoff. The owner could seek a lawful second qualified review, but not claim Yue's relay had already certified it. Yue recorded the accepted pending status and kept the current use restriction visible. The owner's urgent customer date did not make the wood's altered shape match its original task.

shoal_e13_moulds_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_moulds_04.text: A cracked mould held a private maker's mark on its underside. The owner chose proper disposal after an ordinary permitted photograph of that mark for her own record. She did not offer it to the school or a public memorial. Yue witnessed the custody choice without treating the discarded tool as an unowned souvenir. A thing that could no longer work still belonged to someone deciding how much of its history to keep.

shoal_e13_moulds_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_moulds_05.text: The qualified wreck team reached the record-annex cabinet under the now permitted accompanied inventory. Eight original owner bundles were identified by their surviving outer custody record and the cabinet's location. No readable unique annotated surface could be recovered from the burned contents. Basic pattern copies and human skill might remain elsewhere for particular owners, but these eight original annotation surfaces were lost. No hidden ink returned through Yue's circulation.

shoal_e13_moulds_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_moulds_06.text: The custodian who had wanted her key to open the annex saw the actual loss report and chose not to inspect the charred cabinet herself. Her lawful representative completed the accompanied identification. She retained the right to request the offered record under its scope. She did not have to touch blackened paper to make her grief credible. Yue kept the public condition result separate from the private account the woman had not chosen to tell.

shoal_e13_moulds_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_moulds_07.text: One drawing owner had an old base-pattern copy at home. He would use it for a new working note but could not call it the unique revised original lost in the cabinet. Another had no exact copy and planned to ask a colleague about remembered measurements. Their futures differed. The loss report left room for honest reconstruction from actual retained sources, not a blanket claim that the fire had erased every toolmaker's knowledge.

shoal_e13_moulds_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_moulds_08.text: The twenty-eight usable moulds could support current ordinary work where owners still had appropriate benches, material, staff, and accepted orders. Surviving wood did not rebuild the burned workshop around it. One owner chose to take two pieces to an already offered neighboring bench. Another kept hers in finite storage while deciding whether to continue the trade. Yue recorded each actual decision and did not presume everyone wanted the same return to work.

shoal_e13_moulds_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_moulds_09.text: A mould worker asked whether the pending two adaptations could be done with qi. Yue's qualified small application could not certify that wood task. The ordinary reader offered a separately scoped material process and estimated its real time. The owner would need to accept a new funded job. The relay's useful water interval had preserved a possibility, not a technique that made all future skilled labor unnecessary.

shoal_e13_moulds_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_moulds_10.text: At the safe table, two owners allowed a limited public description of surviving dimensions for a future worker comparison. Others declined because their ordinary trade patterns remained private. The reader could use the offered geometry without reproducing unoffered marks. Yue kept the permissions attached to the particular pieces, not to a general rescued-stock category. A community emergency had moved material; it had not made ownership and livelihood disappear.

shoal_e13_moulds_11.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_moulds_11.text: The record owners chose their own next steps after receiving loss confirmation. One requested a private ordinary memory session with a former coworker; another declined new reconstruction until the family decided whether the trade should continue. He Ming could carry offered public requests and not command those decisions. Yue watched the custodian leave with the loss report folded tightly. The paper in her hand now described absence, which was not the same thing as a restored original.

shoal_e13_moulds_12.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_moulds_12.text: Three usable moulds were received by their owners that afternoon under actual identity and custody checks. The remaining stock stayed with the named keeper for its finite accepted storage. The four cracked pieces awaited or completed lawful disposal decisions separately. No uncollected tool became a gift to Yue, and no private pattern became a public diagram by default. The safe line had preserved a count whose next actions still belonged to many people.

shoal_e13_moulds_13.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_moulds_13.text: A public notice stated the exact reviewed states: twenty-eight usable wooden moulds, two pending adaptation, four out of working use, and eight lost original annotated drawing surfaces. It did not announce that every owner was satisfied. The numbers gave the town a real base for new offers, claims, and choices. The fire had spared a working material path and closed a particular documentary one. A new task could use the first without denying the second.

shoal_e13_moulds_14.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_moulds_14.text: Rong asked how many owners could accept a near-term manufacturing order. The reader said physical mould condition did not answer each workshop's staffing or willingness. Owners would need their own offers. Yue liked the answer because it stopped a resource count from swallowing people. Twenty-eight usable tools did not mean twenty-eight available workers, and an ordinary merchant could not get them simply by naming how useful their preserved stock might be to his route.

shoal_e13_moulds_15.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_moulds_15.text: At the end of her receiving interval, Yue filed the actual reviewed conditions and offered owner decisions. Her restricted arm had handled no mould. The eight originals remained lost, while basic sources and skills survived where they actually did. The twenty-eight usable pieces could support accepted work after proper receiving. She had been paid to make those distinctions clear enough for owners to act, not to declare the water role morally superior because its count contained more wood.

shoal_e13_moulds_16.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_moulds_16.text: The record custodian who had declined her explanation before now asked for the public contact of a qualified ordinary reconstruction reader. Yue gave the current offered contact without guaranteeing a result or promising access to a private source. The woman thanked her for that small information and still did not speak about the fire choice. A next interaction could begin before forgiveness, leaving both the lost surfaces and the other group's usable moulds real.

shoal_e13_rejoin_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_rejoin_01.text: The public receiving room did not become quiet when the first condition results were posted. Owners compared current offers, argued about lead times, and asked who could pay new work. Yue's four-hour shift ended while several questions remained. She handed the proper files to the named clerk and left them with their actual states. A paid term could finish one day's work without finishing a person's loss. Tomorrow's receiving would begin from the actual account, not a blank clean page.

shoal_e13_rejoin_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_rejoin_02.text: At the public wall, the worker whose stock had survived in one form or another asked whether she could join a different trade. She was skilled at packing but tired of waiting for a store to provide safe space. He Ming offered the current ordinary apprenticeship contact he knew and no promise of acceptance. She took it and said she would ask after her present orders. A disaster could change a person's preferred work without making her next profession automatic.

shoal_e13_rejoin_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_rejoin_03.text: The two pattern readers disagreed about a proposed material adaptation that an owner offered for later work. One wanted a fuller ordinary measurement; the other thought the available retained specification was enough for a preliminary estimate. They did not resolve it by appealing to Yue's cultivation. She recorded the agreed next information request and left the technical disagreement to its qualified process. Being paid to receive a judgment did not make her the person who could issue every one.

shoal_e13_rejoin_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_rejoin_04.text: One reader asked why her left-handed numbers looked like frightened insects. Yue said they were making a safe crossing while her elbow rested. He laughed and offered a wider ruled page. The change let her separate the actual columns more clearly without stretching the arm. Ordinary accommodation had a physical shape. She accepted it instead of treating the awkward handwriting as proof that a sixth-stage practitioner ought to reject help.

shoal_e13_rejoin_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_rejoin_05.text: The actual tags-and-closures line funded the offered owner labels, current receiving seals, and return container marks within its eighteen copper. It did not purchase rights to copy private patterns. The twelve-copper message line carried the specified receiving notices and accepted owner appointment updates. Han checked that the existing closed restoration and safety accounts were absent from this new ledger. A familiar clerk could make a new paid term easier to staff without making old money available again.

shoal_e13_rejoin_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_rejoin_06.text: On Day Three Hundred Fifteen, the qualified wreck team confirmed a safe current approach to some private-tool locations. Representatives identified pieces under their owners' proper authority. The owner involved in the assault had six steel tools found: two passed ordinary current working checks, one needed separately accepted sharpening, and three had destroyed handles with metal condition still requiring their own review. The count was offered through his lawful representative. It neither vindicated the shove nor erased his genuine loss.

shoal_e13_rejoin_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_rejoin_07.text: His relative received the two usable tools under actual identity checks and kept the pending pieces in their owner-marked process. Yue did not touch them or speak with the man at the table. Her supported arm was visible to the ordinary receiver, who kept the assault matter separate. A bad action had not made every object belonging to its actor unowned. A surviving tool had not made the injured person's body uninjured.

shoal_e13_rejoin_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_rejoin_08.text: At the end of the second shift, a child asked if Yue was now a left-handed clerk forever. She said the current restriction had another review date and nobody had promised the exact day the elbow would feel ordinary. The child said he had once disliked a bandage because it made everyone ask questions. Yue agreed that questions could grow heavy. He showed her a new drawing instead of asking another one, which she appreciated.

shoal_e13_rejoin_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_rejoin_09.text: On Day Three Hundred Sixteen, an owner requested a public copied extract of an offered pattern. The two qualified readers checked the narrow content, and the owner approved it before ordinary copying. The cost came from his separately accepted small copy payment, not from Yue's private purse or a silent excess in the tags line. Other owners' private annotations stayed absent. A useful public resource was being made by an actual consenting person, not released by a rescue volunteer's reputation.

shoal_e13_rejoin_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_rejoin_10.text: The copied extract contained one reversed measurement label from its first setup. A reader caught it before distribution, retained the corrected audit mark, and reprinted that limited line within the copy worker's accepted task. Yue remembered the school block reversed at a lesson and smiled at how ordinary skill still needed checks. The mistake did not turn the pattern into a mystery. It became a precise error repaired before another person's work relied on it.

shoal_e13_rejoin_11.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_rejoin_11.text: That afternoon, Song Mei asked whether a performer could visit the receiving room's public beginning. The keeper said yes under the ordinary capacity and no recording of private owner discussions. She attended briefly and found the room less theatrical than she had expected. 'Everybody keeps waiting for a sentence that makes their tools new,' she told Yue afterward. Yue said some also waited for an actual reader to tell them which old tool could still work. Song Mei accepted the correction.

shoal_e13_rejoin_12.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_rejoin_12.text: The artist wanted a new piece about a fictional room full of questions, but she would not borrow unoffered names or private patterns. She asked Yue about her own ordinary feeling after the first paid receiving days. Yue permitted one personal statement about awkward left-handed numbers and withheld the assault incident from artistic use. The offer stayed narrow. Friendship could support a real piece while protecting an event its owner did not want made public entertainment.

shoal_e13_rejoin_13.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_rejoin_13.text: On Day Three Hundred Seventeen, Yue attended the scheduled ordinary watch hearing after her four-hour receiving shift. The offered witnesses gave their actual views of the shove. The man acknowledged contact and blamed the fire for his anger. The receiver distinguished that explanation from permission to strike. Yue presented her own actual medical fee receipts, six copper incurred by then, without releasing private clinical detail she had not offered.

shoal_e13_rejoin_14.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_rejoin_14.text: The ordinary process directed restitution for the accepted actual clinical costs, up to eight copper if the scheduled later fee was incurred and proved. The man's current means supported a finite two-copper installment arrangement rather than an imaginary instant purse. The first payment date was Three Hundred Eighteen. The decision did not buy Yue's forgiveness or decide his lost-tool compensation. Those questions belonged to different people and processes.

shoal_e13_rejoin_15.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_rejoin_15.text: The man said he was sorry for the shove and still angry about the boundary. Yue accepted the apology as a statement he had made and did not promise the feeling he wanted in return. She asked him not to approach her outside the current process. The watch receiver recorded the applicable contact limit. His lawful representative could continue the tool inventory. Ordinary accountability could be specific enough to protect a person without requiring an elaborate new villain.

shoal_e13_rejoin_16.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_rejoin_16.text: Outside, Yan asked if the hearing had changed her medical restriction. It had not. Yue laughed because the question sounded absurd until she recognized her own wish to stand straighter after a public answer. The bruise still pulled at the elbow. She went home by the ordinary clear route and rested. A valid account could support justice while leaving a body to recover in its own qualified time.

shoal_e13_rejoin_17.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_rejoin_17.text: On Day Three Hundred Eighteen, Han paid the first twenty-five copper from the new receiving account after the five actual performed shifts. Yue received the first two-copper clinical-cost installment through the named watch process separately. It reimbursed part of money already paid; it was not another care fee or a new task wage. She kept the two sources distinct in her own purse note and renewed her lodging for the actual next nights.

shoal_e13_rejoin_18.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_rejoin_18.text: At the lodging table, a traveler mistook the arm support for a training device. Yue said it belonged to an ordinary current care plan. He asked whether wearing one would strengthen his qi. She said no and recommended the appropriate qualified instruction process for his actual practice question. The traveler looked disappointed, then relieved that he would not need to buy a strange object before sleeping. The town kept making rumors from things it could see without knowing their purpose.

shoal_e13_rejoin_19.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_rejoin_19.text: Yue spent the first rest day at the public beach with no load or powered practice. She set the imperfect cup on a flat stone and drank ordinary water. The shore keeper was coordinating a permitted lost-net cleanup elsewhere under its actual route and weather limits. It would not retrieve the dead seal. A current effort could be useful without revising the past. She let the quiet hold that fact rather than writing a consolation for it.

shoal_e13_rejoin_20.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_rejoin_20.text: On Day Three Hundred Twenty, the pattern readers prepared next week's offered review work with the current owner permissions attached. The qualified metal checks and wood adaptations were not all completed yet. Yue had no shift that day and did not volunteer unpaid hours to shorten every wait. Her paid term named actual days and tasks. Resting a restricted elbow was part of remaining able to perform them, not an offense against people whose impatience she understood.

shoal_e13_rejoin_21.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_rejoin_21.text: He Ming came to the public board with a revised question about supplier summaries and actual loading states. The earlier public or confidential receiving had created different permitted source paths. He would ask the relevant owners again before a later challenge used any detail. Yue could offer her own outside dates and no unseen inside claim. The known lamp spill witnesses had their own statements to preserve. Their evidence would not become hers merely because she had been injured near the wreck.

shoal_e13_rejoin_22.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_rejoin_22.text: At the clinic door, the leg-injured worker's partner asked Yue where the public message desk would stand next week. She wanted to coordinate an accepted care journey without making the worker's full plan public. Yue showed the current contact and hours within her offered ordinary receiving role. The partner thanked her and said the worker was tired of being called lucky. He was glad to be alive and still had a leg that hurt and a trade he could not presently resume.

shoal_e13_rejoin_23.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_rejoin_23.text: Yue understood the complaint differently after the elbow. Her bruise was smaller and its plan shorter, but she disliked a stranger describing it as a fine lesson. She could receive the partner's offered sentence without pretending their conditions matched. The worker's finite care deposit would need actual sessions and current checks. Her own private fee receipts did not authorize her to supervise his plan. They went to their separate desks.

shoal_e13_rejoin_24.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_rejoin_24.text: On Day Three Hundred Twenty-One, the ordinary practitioner performed Yue's actual next review. She paid the stated two-copper fee from received money. Touch, grip, and leg checks matched her prior narrow baseline, and the elbow's tenderness had eased enough for permitted ordinary waist tasks under the stated limits. The old shoulder still excluded overhead work. No new cultivation stage or broader powered application had been examined here.

shoal_e13_rejoin_25.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_rejoin_25.text: The practitioner ended the temporary no-load restriction within that current clearance and warned against treating relief as proof she should catch falling weight. Powered work would still require its qualified setup and current readiness; she planned none today. Her two follow-up fees brought the actual assault-related care total to eight, following the initial four. The watch process could reimburse only that documented total, with later installments paid on their real dates.

shoal_e13_rejoin_26.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_rejoin_26.text: Yue returned to her second working week's first receiving shift with the arm no longer supported in the same way. She still used the wider page because it was helpful. The ordinary readers did not celebrate by assigning a heavy crate. Her job remained reading offered decisions and witnessed custody. The new body state could make a small task easier without changing every role the town had accepted for her.

shoal_e13_rejoin_27.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_rejoin_27.text: A pattern owner asked if she would now demonstrate the marker talisman in his workroom. She declined the unscheduled application. The school had qualified one bounded corrected setup, and today's clinical review did not qualify another. The owner accepted a future public school contact instead. Ordinary restraint felt less like a declaration of humility and more like keeping the actual facts from acquiring abilities nobody had tested.

shoal_e13_rejoin_28.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_rejoin_28.text: At the end of the shift, the receiving room had a second week's proper files and several genuine pending owner decisions. Some work resources had survived; other exact surfaces and tools had not. The qualified readers could offer new comparison and reconstruction, not resurrection of consumed material. Yue handed the day record to Han, with the body review completed and her current limits understood. The fire's human care would continue on different schedules.

shoal_e13_rejoin_29.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_rejoin_29.text: Song Mei met her briefly at the public lane and asked whether the arm felt less bad. Yue said yes within the current plan, and the artist accepted the qualified answer without demanding optimism. They talked about a new pear shipment whose fruit had arrived hard enough to disappoint every seller. The ordinary subject felt like a kindness. A friendship could acknowledge an injury and then spend its offered minutes on something else.

shoal_e13_rejoin_30.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_rejoin_30.text: The next day's public receiving would include the leg-injured worker's accepted care logistics and current restricted-income terms. Yue's role would concern offered messages and dates, not diagnosis or treatment choice. Qualified clinicians, the worker, and his partner would do that work. She read the public appointment time and stopped there. Her own recovered elbow did not make another body's longer course less urgent or easier.

shoal_e13_rejoin_31.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_rejoin_31.text: The safe custody and loss counts remained with the owners who would build their next work around them. The record path and the mould path had preserved different possibilities through the fire. Neither could be made identical by a generous new offer. Yue walked home carrying her ordinary paid job, the current body clearance, and an imperfect cup that still needed turning to sit level. Tomorrow would ask how care was actually funded and performed after rescue.

shoal_e13_drawing_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_drawing_01.text: On the school board, an student drawing showed Yue beside the tipped lamp inside Shed Six. The student had imagined a view he did not possess and labeled it a witnessed reconstruction. Yue asked him to check the public account. She had stood outside the rope and heard the first shout. He changed the label to an imagined scene, then chose to draw the alarm route separately from the facts.

shoal_e13_drawing_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e13_drawing_02.text: His new route drawing put the public boundary farther from the shed than his picture had shown. It looked less heroic and made the safe movement clearer. The teacher accepted both pages with their different labels, leaving imagination and evidence room to serve different purposes. Yue thanked the student for the correction and did not demand a flattering replacement. Her body had been outside the flame, and that was enough to show.
